$comment: The values the research harness would otherwise hard-code in several modules. common.py reads this file; a change here is a change of the whole harness. remote and base_branch name the git remote and the branch a run lands on; github_repo is the repository every gh call names with --repo, so gh never resolves a remote of the checkout; public_repo is the repository whose issues rq intake reads and whose data/meta.json rq publish-status reads; capture_cutover is the first evidence date that needs a capture and a quote (rule C21); probe_capture_cutover is the first date from which a probe: row needs them too (a stored probe record, rq capture --probe); lease_hours is how long a work lease of a unit that is not integrated yet lives (an integrated unit's held lease and a landed run's review lease hold until the merge or the close), and how long a session folder with no change counts as live; claim_hours is how long a claim of an rq:research issue (rq open --issue N) holds with no pull request. git_network_timeout_s is how long a git fetch or push may run before the harness treats it as hung, kills it with its transport helper and fails it, and how long a transfer may stall below one byte a second (a guard against a dead connection, not a pace). ci_repo and ci_workflow name the public repository whose Actions run the heavy checks of a pull request (the gate comparison, the render check, the selftests, the parity check) on one head, and its workflow; ci_ref is the branch that holds that workflow, and ci_jobs the jobs whose success makes a run green (scripts/research/ci.py). There is no request rate here: the harness sets no client-side cap (AGENTS.md section 2 rule 15).
